clue.text: Machine used in too many designs, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that a single machine turns up in far too many design projects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters sitting inside 'too many designs', and 'on reflection' says read them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator is a machine used to make electricity, and the dynamo is the classic example.

clue.text: Ties involving football player in difficulties

indicators.note: involving means including, so the ties wrap round the player

parts.note: draws are tied matches
a back is a defensive football player

explanation.surface: A football team keeps drawing because one defender is struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawbacks are disadvantages or problems, the snags that make things hard.

clue.text: Excellent area, nothing less, to climb in African country

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI

indicators.note: less says the letter for nothing is taken away

parts.note: a region is an area
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A fine area, with nothing missing, that climbers visit in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: AI REGION loses an O (from 'nothing less') to give AIREGIN, and 'to climb' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a large nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Planet hardly expressing content of a boggy nature

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun

indicators.note: to express is to squeeze out, so the inside of hardly is pressed out leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A planet barely showing any boggy content on its surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressing' means squeezing out, as juice is expressed, so 'hardly' loses ARDL to leave H and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is wet and spongy, the same quality as a bog.

clue.text: Recalled quote about piece of film depicting zodiacal region

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other, here the reversed word wrapping the film piece
recalled is taken as called back, so the word for quote is read from the end

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it
a clip is a short extract from a film

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a line quoted about a film clip showing the signs of the zodiac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' means called back, so the quote is read in reverse; 'about' then wraps it round the film piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecliptic is the sun's apparent yearly path, and the zodiac is the band of sky straddling it.

clue.text: Like some rhythms around bed, though cutting volume

parts.note: circa means around, as in dates

indicators.note: cutting volume means the letter for volume is cut out

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed

explanation.surface: Some rhythms surround a bed, though they turn down the volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Circadian rhythms are the body's roughly daily cycles of sleep and waking.

clue.text: Vaguely intrigued about a twit's latest churlishness

indicators.note: vaguely says the letters are put loosely into a new order
latest picks the final letter of twit's

explanation.surface: Someone is mildly curious about a fool's most recent rude behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaguely' shuffles INTRIGUED, A and T (the end of twit's).
explanation.definitionFit: Ingratitude is a failure to give thanks, a churlish lack of grace.

clue.text: Cause petrification? Fellow doing for hill in region

indicators.note: doing for means standing in for, so the fellow replaces the hill

parts.note: a territory is a region
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A man killing off a hill somewhere would scare people stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing for' reads as killing but here means replacing. A tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To be petrified is to be frozen with fear, so causing it means frightening someone.

clue.text: Small group ignoring taxmen for year in repeated sequence of events

indicators.note: ignoring says the taxmen are left out of the group
for says the year is put in the place of the taxmen

parts.note: a circle is a small group of associates
IR stands for Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: A small group dodges the taxman for a year, a pattern that keeps repeating.
explanation.walkthrough: IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax office.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is a series of events that recurs regularly, like the seasons.

clue.text: A facade, eliminating old recess

indicators.note: eliminating means removing, so the letter for old goes

parts.note: a pose is a pretence, a false front

explanation.surface: A building's front wall is taken down, removing an old alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facade' looks architectural, like the definition, but means a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted semicircular alcove, usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Threat to bump off daughter? That gets you upset

indicators.note: bump off means kill, so the daughter is removed from the word for threat

parts.note: a danger is a threat

explanation.surface: A menacing threat to murder someone's daughter would understandably leave you upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works with the answer read as a verb: something that angers you is what upsets you.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke fury in someone is to upset them, so the verb sense matches the phrase.

clue.text: Painkiller: cut to vanish, sprain to reduce

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
to go can mean to disappear, as in 'the pain has gone'

indicators.note: reduce says the word for sprain is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: a rick is a sprain or wrench of a joint

explanation.surface: Instructions for a painkiller that makes a cut vanish and a sprain shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: Paregoric is an old opium-based medicine used to relieve pain and settle the stomach.

clue.text: French vessel bearing nothing of ornate design

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the vessel holds the letter for nothing

parts.note: barque is a sailing ship, the word taken from French
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A French ship carries no cargo but is elaborately decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque describes the richly decorated, elaborate style of 17th-century art and architecture.

clue.text: Mostly sickly, suffering, beset by palpitation — mercury?

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the quiver goes round the shuffled letters

parts.note: a quiver is a trembling or flutter, like a palpitation

indicators.note: suffering signals the letters are knocked into a new order
mostly says the last letter of sickly is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone sickly and ill with heart flutters asks whether the thermometer's reading is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of sickly, 'suffering' shuffles the rest, and 'beset by' sets them inside the tremor word.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver is the old name for mercury, the liquid metal; the question mark nods to the god.

clue.text: America mostly changed, accommodating constant greed

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the shortened word takes in the constant
mostly says the word for changed loses its final letter

parts.note: something changed has varied
c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light, a constant

explanation.surface: A comment that America has largely changed but kept its constant greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America mostly' looks like one unit but 'mostly' belongs to 'changed': A, then VARIE(D) holding C.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth, a direct synonym for greed.

clue.text: Cleaner about to contend with nearly all current racket

indicators.note: about says the word for cleaner goes round the shortened rival

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning lady

indicators.note: nearly all says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to rival someone is to contend with them
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A cleaner is about to face nearly all of some ongoing din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to', but 'about' is the container round the shortened rival. A char is a British cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade, so the word has come to mean a din or racket.

clue.text: A large cry of pain, gripped by stomachache related to booze

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside, so the cry sits within the stomachache

parts.note: colic is severe abdominal pain
oh is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A loud groan from someone with a stomachache brought on by drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholic describes anything containing or connected with alcoholic drink.

clue.text: No time for neat lines in poem

indicators.note: no time says the letter for time is dropped from the word for neat

parts.note: neat means tidy
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Someone without time to write neat lines in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short poem describing a peaceful pastoral scene.

clue.text: Element in US city manhunt resolved

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: resolved means sorted out, so the letters of manhunt are reworked

explanation.surface: A police search in an American city is finally brought to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanthanum is a chemical element, a soft silvery metal of the rare earths.

clue.text: Ogre — one lets out fearful cry? On the contrary

indicators.note: lets out means releases, so the word for one is taken out of the cry

parts.note: a shriek is a cry of fear
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ogre is someone who makes others scream in fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the roles: not one letting out a cry but the cry letting out one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrek is the green ogre of the animated films and the children's book behind them.

clue.text: Later exam not quite scheduled for the last few participants?

indicators.note: not quite says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a resit is a second attempt at an exam, taken later
due means expected or scheduled

explanation.surface: A resit timetabled for the final stragglers who still need to take it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: the residue is whatever remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is a remainder, so the few people left at the end can be called it.

clue.text: Not supporting nuclear power process, expressing bafflement

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
fusion is the joining of atomic nuclei that releases energy

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to fusion power voices their puzzlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bewildered and unable to make sense of things is a state of bafflement.

clue.text: Keen on a thing involving choir's ultimate choral piece

indicators.note: involving means including, so the phrase takes in the choir's last letter

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: ultimate picks the final letter of choir's

parts.note: it can stand for a thing

explanation.surface: Someone keen on an item that features a choir's last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or anthem sung at the start of a church service.

clue.text: Desire to restrain venomous creature with a sting?

indicators.note: restrain means hold in, so the wish holds the creature

parts.note: a wish is a desire
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Someone wants to hold back a venomous creature that stings.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means sharp-tongued, its remarks carrying a sting like the insect.

clue.text: Promise to retain latitude for globe

indicators.note: retain means keep inside, so the promise holds the latitude letter

parts.note: to give one's word is to promise

explanation.surface: A pledge to keep some latitude across the whole globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe is the earth, the planet as a whole.

clue.text: Fast runner, champion, to dislike going round after end of race

indicators.note: after puts the reversed dislike behind the end of race
end of picks the final letter of race
going round says the word for dislike is turned back to front

parts.note: to hate is to dislike

explanation.surface: A champion sprinter resents having to run another lap after the race ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses the word for dislike, and 'after' places it behind the last letter of race.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is the fastest land animal, famous for its sprinting.

clue.text: Work in church producing garment for priest

indicators.note: in places the work inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Work in a church yields a vestment for the priest.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A cope is a long cloak-like vestment worn by clergy in processions.

clue.text: Crimson wrap needing no new further design

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red

indicators.note: needing no says the letter for new is dropped

parts.note: to envelop is to wrap

explanation.surface: A crimson wrap is so good it needs no further redesign.
explanation.definitionFit: To redevelop is to plan and build again, taking a design a stage further.

clue.text: Small quantity of old jokes getting disdainful response?

parts.note: corn is trite, old-fashioned humour

explanation.surface: A few stale jokes get a sniffy reaction from the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt shown openly is the typical disdainful reaction to something.

clue.text: See 3
Food, full-flavoured, for old film star

parts.note: diet is the food one eats
rich food is heavy and full of flavour

explanation.surface: A review praising rich, flavourful food that suits a veteran actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-American actress of Hollywood's golden era.

clue.text: Limits to security support process

indicators.note: limits are the edges, so take the first and last letters of security

parts.note: a stem supports a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: Security budgets are capped so a support process can run.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised method or procedure, so it can mean a process.
